title: Runtime config + feature flag wiring for kernel selector v2 (tier/region enablement, per-model overrides, kill switch)
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
Scope
- Wire config + feature flags for kernel selector v2 such that we can:
  1) enable/disable selector v2 by tier and region
  2) pin/override selection per model (family and/or exact model id)
  3) flip an emergency kill switch that deterministically falls back to selector v1 (or safe kernel set) without requiring a runtime redeploy

Context
Selector v2 is table-driven and can regress tail latency or correctness (NaN/shape edge cases) if an entry is wrong. We need explicit rollout controls to:
- stage enablement (internal -> canary -> prod)
- quickly rollback by region/tier
- hotfix specific model families with overrides while leaving v2 enabled for others

Proposed configuration surface (runtime)
1) Top-level switch
- runtime.kernel_selector.mode: "v1" | "v2" | "auto" (default "auto" in code, but we will ship config defaulted to "v1" until rollout)
- runtime.kernel_selector.kill_switch: boolean (default false)
  - If true: forces v1 regardless of any other config. This is the emergency lever.

2) Enablement policy (tier + region)
- runtime.kernel_selector.v2_enablement_rules: ordered list of rules evaluated first-match
  - fields: tier, region, percent, selector_version
  - selector_version: "v1" | "v2"
  - percent: 0-100 stable hash on (request_tenant_id, model_id) so it is sticky and debuggable

3) Overrides (per model family / model id)
- runtime.kernel_selector.overrides: ordered list evaluated before enablement rules
  - match fields:
    - model_family (e.g., llama, mistral, qwen, unknown)
    - model_id (exact string match; optional)
    - gpu_sku (optional; e.g., L4, A10, A100, H100)
    - seq_bucket (optional)
  - action fields:
    - selector_version: "v1" | "v2"
    - force_kernel_id: string (optional; only allowed for debug/internal tiers)
    - allow_kernel_ids: comma-separated string (optional; used for safety)

Precedence rules (must be deterministic)
1) kill_switch == true => selector v1
2) override match (first-match) => apply override
3) enablement rules match (first-match) => select v1/v2
4) default => v1 (during rollout), then later v2 once declared stable

Rollout requirements
- Hosted:
  - allow per-region staged rollout (us-east-1 first)
  - allow percent-based cohorts
- Dedicated:
  - cluster-level config can opt-in to v2, plus per-model overrides for evaluations
- Private:
  - maintain backwards compatible config keys; unknown keys ignored; safe defaults to v1

Safety + validation
- Runtime should log a single-line boot summary of resolved config (redacting any sensitive IDs), including:
  - default mode, kill_switch state
  - count of enablement rules and overrides loaded
  - config version/hash
- Config validation on load:
  - reject invalid enum values
  - reject percent outside [0,100]
  - validate override ordering doesn’t create ambiguous outcomes (warn only; do not crash)
- Emit selector decision telemetry (already tracked in ENG-3927) annotated with:
  - selector_version
  - reason: kill_switch | override | rule | default
  - rule_id / override_id (bucketed)

Acceptance criteria
- We can enable v2 for: tier=hosted-canary, region=us-east-1, percent=5, without redeploy
- We can force v1 for a specific model family (e.g., qwen) while leaving v2 enabled elsewhere
- We can flip kill switch globally and see v1 decisions within 5 minutes (config propagation SLO)
- Precedence is covered by unit tests + a small integration test
- Backward compatibility: runtime-1.18 ignores new keys, runtime-1.19 defaults to v1 unless explicitly enabled

Implementation notes
- Use config loader shared path with other runtime flags; keep schema in one place.
- Stable hashing: use existing request hashing utility (same as traffic shaping) to avoid new behavior.
- Force-kernel-id should be gated: only allowed when tier in {internal, hosted-canary} to avoid customers pinning arbitrary kernels without support.

Links
- Design: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/kernel-auto-selection-v2-design.json
- Related PR (expected): sources/github/redwood/pr_18480_selector_v2_feature_flag_and_overrides.json
- Rollout execution: ENG-3934
comments: 2026-01-23 (Benji Okafor): Drafted config schema + precedence rules. Open question: do we want both mode and enablement_rules? Proposal: keep mode for simple cluster-wide pin, rules for hosted rollout. Mode becomes an override at the top (after kill switch).

2026-01-27 (Connor O'Brien): Please ensure kill switch is a single boolean that can be toggled by Release Eng without editing multiple rule entries. Also need sticky percent rollout (hash), not random sampling per request.

2026-01-29 (Sofia Ivanova): Scheduler will pass seq_bucket; overrides should be able to match on bucket but shouldn’t be required. Suggest optional match fields as you wrote. Also please ensure selection remains deterministic if seq_bucket missing (treat as "unknown").

2026-02-01 (Allison Grant): Observability requirement: reason + rule/override identifiers must be emitted but must be cardinality-safe. Please bucket identifiers (e.g., rule_0..rule_n) rather than raw strings. Also need a boot-time log of config hash/version for incident response.

2026-02-04 (Grace Kim): +1 to gating force_kernel_id for internal/canary only. We should assume Dedicated customers will want to pin selector version, not specific kernel ids, unless under support guidance.

2026-02-07 (Benji Okafor): Implemented loader + validation + precedence unit tests. Added stable hash cohorting by (tenant_id, model_id). Added allowlist-only support for force_kernel_id and wired it behind tier check. Sharing PR for review.

2026-02-11 (Connor O'Brien): Reviewed PR. Requested one change: ensure kill switch is evaluated before reading registry so we don’t fail-open if registry parse fails. Also please add metrics for config parse errors (counter) + fallback-to-v1 reason.

2026-02-14 (Benji Okafor): Addressed review: kill switch short-circuits registry load; parse errors increment runtime_config_errors_total{component="kernel_selector"} and default to v1. Added integration test for "invalid override enum" => warning + continue.
2026-02-18 (Mateo Alvarez): Sign-off for runtime-1.19: kill switch + per-family override are mandatory. Thanks for keeping the rollback path simple for SRE/Release.

2026-02-20 (Benji Okafor): Landed and verified in staging: rule-based enablement works; kill switch propagates in ~2-3 min. Next: rollout checklist will reference these keys (ENG-3934) and runbook will document override precedence.
